def drive(me, enemy, arena):
    # Calculate bearing and distance to the enemy
    bearing = bearing_to(enemy.x, enemy.y)
    dist = distance_to(enemy.x, enemy.y)
    
    # Aggressive pursuit logic with distance management
    # If we are too far, move forward and turn toward the enemy
    if dist > 0.6:
        # Turn left if bearing is positive, right if negative
        # To turn left, right wheel must push more than left wheel
        left = 1.0 - (bearing / 180.0)
        right = 1.0 + (bearing / 180.0)
    # If we are too close, back up slightly to avoid being pinned or pushed
    elif dist < 0.4:
        # To turn left while moving backward, the right wheel must move backward more
        left = -1.0 + (bearing / 180.0)
        right = -1.0 - (bearing / 180.0)
    else:
        # Maintain position and keep heading aligned
        left = 0.0 - (bearing / 180.0)
        right = 0.0 + (bearing / 180.0)
        
    # Clamp values to [-1, 1]
    left = max(-1.0, min(1.0, left))
    right = max(-1.0, min(1.0, right))
    
    return (left, right)

def weapons(me, enemy, arena):
    commands = []
    
    # Always keep the horizontal spinner running at maximum speed for maximum damage
    if "front" in me.weapons:
        spinner = me.weapons["front"]
        commands.append(spin("front", spinner["max_rpm"]))
        
    # The robot is invertible, so it can drive while upside down.
    # self_right() is not supported by spinners, so we rely on invertibility.
        
    return commands
